correctness.rationale: The smooth integral nestohedron and tree-rotation graph fix the domain; the blow-up invariant-curve calculation gives epsilon at each fixed point as minimal incident lattice edge length. Direct Loday coordinate differences give ac times a primitive root vector. The deepest-cherry lemma proves 1<=epsilon<=2. The disjoint forbidden-root decomposition proves A=z(G-A) and G=1+z(G^2-2A), hence the unique algebraic generating function. The cut-width argument and Ito Theorem 1.1 prove dense-torus n-1. The embedded standard-library verifier exhaustively checks all trees through n=8 and the series through n=11; finite checks do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The natural local positivity invariant is classified at every torus fixed point in an infinite sequence of smooth projective toric varieties, and the exact dimension-by-dimension distribution satisfies a new nontrivial algebraic tree-count equation. Compared with Ito’s known dense-orbit n-1 result, the bounded fixed-point range displays an unbounded geometric local-positivity gap. This is a structural classification of a motivating natural family, not an arbitrary small numerical slice.
